t: You're at the site of St John Zachary, a church on the north side of Gresham Street, first mentioned in records in 1181. It was destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666 and never rebuilt, and today the site is a garden, first made by fire watchers in 1941. One of its vicars, from 1424, was William Byngham, who founded England's first teacher training college. Nicholas Twyford, a goldsmith who served as Lord Mayor of London, is buried here. He died in 1391.
